newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan Housing Bank sells 50pct of hotel.
newsitem.headline: Jordan Housing Bank sells 50pct of hotel.

text.p: Jordan's Housing Bank, the country's second largest bank, has concluded a deal to sell half of its fully owned five-star Forte Grand hotel to a group of Gulf Arab investors, banking sources said on Thursday.
They said the Jordanian government, which is a minority shareholder in the bank, has approved the sale of the 50 percent stake in the 306-room five star hotel.
The hotel is managed by global hotel chain Forte-Le Meridien.
Housing Bank officials declined to disclose the cost of the deal but financial analysts estimate the total assets of the hotel at around 30 million dinars ($42 million).
The bank remains the largest single, non-government investor on Jordan's stock market. It also has extensive holdings in a wide range of industrial and real estate firms.
Housing Bank's total assets stood at 1.136 billion dinars by the end of 1996 and its deposits stood at 918 million dinars.

It is Jordan's second largest bank and its shareholders include Arab and foreign investors. The government of Kuwait has a 20 percent stake and Oman, Qatar and Iran each have six percent stakes by. Jordan's government owns 18 percent.
